query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Pre-depositing a thin Ti-based coating on tungsten particles in a W–Cu composite will promote the formation of an in-situ Ti-rich interfacial layer during consolidation, which mitigates phase separation and void formation and thereby improves thermal conductivity under high heat-flux and irradiation conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: A W–Cu composite comprising tungsten particles or interconnected tungsten ligaments embedded in a copper matrix that, when processed under conventional conditions, exhibits phase separation and interfacial void formation.
generation.intervention: Apply a thin Ti (or Ti/Ni) coating onto the tungsten particles (e.g., via physical vapor deposition) before composite consolidation (such as spark plasma sintering).
generation.conditions: Processing via spark plasma sintering under conditions relevant for fusion plasma-facing applications, followed by exposure to high heat flux and irradiation regimes similar to those encountered in joints between W-based plasma-facing components and Cu-based cooling parts.
generation.structural_mediator: An in-situ formed, Ti-rich interfacial layer (possibly containing controlled intermetallic phases or solid solutions) at the tungsten–copper interface.
generation.mechanism: The Ti coating reduces interfacial energy and alleviates thermal expansion mismatch between W and Cu. This leads to better metallurgical bonding during sintering, suppressing the phase separation and void formation that ordinarily disrupt electron and phonon transport across the interface.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to an untreated composite, the Ti-coated composite will exhibit fewer interfacial voids, a more integrated microstructure, and consequently higher effective thermal conductivity when subjected to heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.baseline: An untreated W–Cu composite that, under identical processing and service conditions, demonstrates phase separation with interfacial voids which degrade its thermal conductivity.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected if the coating is optimized (in terms of thickness and uniformity) so that it forms a continuous interfacial layer without generating excessive, less-conductive reaction products. The benefit is confined to processing conditions where Ti is active in forming such an interphase without complete interdiffusion that might otherwise degrade conductivity.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of thermal conductivity enhancement is uncertain and may depend on the exact coating parameters and the reaction kinetics during sintering; there is also potential for adverse effects if the coating is too thick or reacts excessively.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of W–Cu composites using identical processing parameters: one set with tungsten particles pre-coated with a thin Ti-based layer and one set without any coating. Subject both sets to spark plasma sintering followed by accelerated heat-flux and irradiation testing that simulates the service environment of plasma-facing joints.
measurements: Thermal conductivity measurements (e.g., via laser flash analysis or non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations)
Microstructural characterization (SEM/TEM) of the W–Cu interface to assess the presence of phase separation and void formation
Irradiation damage evaluation via surface morphology and compositional analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ti-coated composites do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in interfacial voids and phase separation, or fail to show improved thermal conductivity under the same heat-transfer and irradiation conditions compared with the uncoated control samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.
